questions.stem: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2} - 3x + r = 0$ and $\frac{\alpha}{2}, 2\beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2} + 3x + r = 0$. If the roots of the equation $x^{2} + 6x = m$ are $2\alpha + \beta + 2r$ and $\alpha - 2\beta - \frac{r}{2}$, then m is equal to:
questions.solution:
$x^{2} - 3x + r = 0$ has roots $\alpha$, $\beta$
$\alpha + \beta = 3$ .........(i)
$\alpha\beta = r$ ..........(ii)
$x^{2} + 3x + r = 0$ has roots $\alpha/2$, $2\beta$
$\frac{\alpha}{2} + 2\beta = -3$ .........(iii)
From (i) and (iii)
$\alpha = 6,\ \beta = -3$
and from (ii)
$r = -18$
Now
$x^{2} + 6x - m = 0$ has roots $2\alpha + \beta + 2r$ and $\alpha - 2\beta - \frac{r}{2}$
$2\alpha + \beta + 2r = -27$
and $\alpha - 2\beta - \frac{r}{2} = 21$
so $-m = (-27)(21)$
$\Rightarrow m = 567$

questions.stem: Let the circles $C_1 : |z| = r$ and $C_2 : |z - 3 - 4i| = 5$, $z \in \mathbf{C}$, be such that $C_2$ lies within $C_1$. If $z_1$ moves on $C_1$, $z_2$ moves on $C_2$ and $\min|z_1 - z_2| = 2$, then $\max|z_1 - z_2|$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
(See figure: $C_2$ with centre $(3, 4)$ inside $C_1$; the line through O(0,0) and $(3, 4)$ meets $C_1$ at R and Q and $C_2$ at O and P, with $OR = 12$, radius 5 and $PQ = 2$.)
$\text{Max}\,|z_1 - z_2| = OR + OP$
$= 12 + 5 + 5$
$= 22$

questions.stem:
If the system of equations
$x + 5y + 6z = 4,$
$2x + 3y + 4z = 7,$
$x + 6y + az = b$
has infinitely many solutions, then the point $(a, b)$ lies on the line :
questions.solution:
$x + 5y + 6z = 4$
$2x + 3y + 4z = 7$
$x + 6y + az = b$
$D = 0 \Rightarrow \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 5 & 6 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 6 & a \end{vmatrix} = 0$

questions.stem: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots\ldots$ be an A.P. and $g_1 = a_1, g_2, g_3, \ldots\ldots$ be an increasing G.P. If $a_1 = a_2 + g_2 = 1$ and $a_3 + g_3 = 4$, then $a_{10} + g_5$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $a_1 = g_1$, $a = 1$
$a_2 = 1 + d$, $\quad a_3 = 1 + 2d$
$g_2 = r$, $\quad g_3 = r^{2}$
Now, $a_2 + g_2 = 1$
$\Rightarrow 1 + d + r = 1$
$\Rightarrow d + r = 0 \quad \Rightarrow d = -r$
and $a_3 + g_3 = 4$
$\Rightarrow 1 + 2d + r^{2} = 4$
put $d = -r$
$\Rightarrow (r - 1)^{2} = 4$
$\Rightarrow r - 1 = \pm 2$
$\Rightarrow r = 3, -1$
$r = 3$ for increassing GP
$d = -3$
Now $a_{10} + g_5$
$= 1 + 9d + r^{4}$
$= 1 - 27 + 81$
$= 55$

questions.stem: If for $3 \le r \le 30$, $\left({}^{30}C_{30-r}\right) + 3\left({}^{30}C_{31-r}\right) + 3\left({}^{30}C_{32-r}\right) + \left({}^{30}C_{33-r}\right) = {}^{m}C_{r}$ then m equals :
Let $P_n$ denote the total number of triangles formed by joining the vertices of an n–side regular polygon. If $P_{n+1} - P_n = 66$ then the sum of all distinct prime divisors of n is :
questions.solution:
$P_n = {}^{n}C_{3}$
$\Rightarrow P_{n+1} - P_n = 66$
$\Rightarrow {}^{n+1}C_{3} - {}^{n}C_{3} = 66$
$\Rightarrow \frac{(n+1) \cdot n \cdot (n-1)}{6} - \frac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6} = 66$
$\Rightarrow n(n-1).3 = 6\ .\ 66$
$\Rightarrow n(n-1) = 132$
$\Rightarrow n^{2} - n - 132 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (n - 12)(n + 11) = 0$
$\Rightarrow n = 12, \quad n = -11$ (Rejected)
Now
sum of prime diviser of 12
$= 2 + 3 = 5$

questions.stem: A man throws a fair coin repeatedly. He gets 10 points for each head he throws and 5 points for each tail he throws. If the probability that he gets exactly 30 points is $\frac{m}{n}$ where $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, then $m + n$ is equal to :

The mean and variance of n observations are 8 and 16, respectively. If the sum of the first $(n - 1)$ observations is 48 and the sum of squares of the first $(n - 1)$ observations is 496, then the value of n is :
questions.solution:
$\frac{(x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_{n-1}) + x_n}{n} = 8$
$\Rightarrow 48 + x_n = 8n$
$\Rightarrow x_n = 8(n - 6)$ .........(i)
and $\frac{x_1^{2} + x_2^{2} + \cdots + x_{n-1}^{2} + x_n^{2}}{n} - 64 = 16$
$\Rightarrow 496 + x_n^{2} = 80n$
$\Rightarrow x_n^{2} = 80n - 496$ .......(ii)
from (1) and (ii)
$64(n - 6)^{2} = 16(5n - 31)$
$\Rightarrow 4(n^{2} - 12n + 36) = 5n - 31$
$\Rightarrow 4n^{2} - 53n + 175 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (4n - 25)(n - 7) = 0$
$\Rightarrow n = 7,\ n = \frac{25}{4} \notin N$

questions.stem: Let a circle pass through the origin and its centre be the point of intersection of two mutually perpendicular lines $x + (k - 1)y + 3 = 0$ and $2x + k^{2}y - 4 = 0$. If the line $x - y + 2 = 0$ intersects the circle at the points A and B, then $(AB)^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$x + (k - 1)y + 3 = 0$
and $2x + k^{2}y - 4 = 0$
lines are perpendicular so
$\left(\frac{-1}{k-1}\right)\left(\frac{-2}{k^{2}}\right) = -1$
$\Rightarrow k^{3} - k^{2} = -2$
$\Rightarrow k = -1$
so lines are
$x - 2y + 3 = 0$
and $2x + y - 4 = 0$
POI is $(1, 2)$ which is centre
Circe passes through origin so $r = \sqrt{5}$
Equation of circle
$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2x - 4y = 0$
solving it with line
$y = x + 2$
gives
$x^{2} + (x + 2)^{2} - 2x - 4(x + 2) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} + x^{2} + 4x + 4 - 2x - 4x - 8 = 0$
$\Rightarrow 2x^{2} - 2x - 4 = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} - x - 2 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (x - 2)(x + 1) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x = -1, 2$
so points $A(-1, 1)$ and $B(2, 4)$
$AB = \sqrt{18} \Rightarrow AD^{2} = 18$

questions.stem: Let O be the origin, and P and Q be two points on the rectangular hyperbola $xy = 12$ such that the mid point of the line segment PQ is $\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)$ Then the area of the triangle OPQ equals :
questions.solution:
$\left(t, \frac{12}{t}\right)$ —— $\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-1}{2}\right)$ —— $\left(P, \frac{12}{P}\right)$
$\frac{t + p}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{12}{t} + \frac{12}{p} = -1$
$\Rightarrow t + P = 1$ ..........(i)
$\Rightarrow \frac{t + p}{tp} = -\frac{1}{12}$
$\Rightarrow tP = -12$ ..........(ii)
From (i) and (ii)
$t = 4, P = -3$
so $P(4, 3)$ and $Q(-3, -4)$
Area of $\Delta OPQ = \left|\frac{1}{2}\begin{vmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 & 1 \\ -3 & -4 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\right|$
$= \left|\frac{1}{2}(-16 + 9)\right| = \frac{7}{2}$

questions.stem: Let the parabola $y = x^{2} + px + q$ passing through the point $(1, -1)$ be such that the distance between its vertex and the x-axis is minimum. Then the value of $p^{2} + q^{2}$ is :
questions.solution:
$y = x^{2} + px + q$
$(1, -1)$ satisfies it
$-1 = 1 + p + q \Rightarrow p + q = -2$
Co-ordinate of vertex $\left(-\frac{p}{2}, -\frac{(p^{2} - 4q)}{4}\right)$
$= \left(-\frac{p}{2}, -\frac{(p^{2} + 4p + 4)}{4}\right)$
distance of vertex from x-axis
$= \left|\frac{4 + p^{2} + 4p}{4}\right| = \left|\frac{(p + 2)^{2}}{4}\right|$
minimum distance $= 0$ when $p = -2$
so $p = -2 \quad \Rightarrow q = 0$
$p^{2} + q^{2} = 4$

questions.stem: Let $P = \{\theta \in [0, 4\pi] : \tan^{2}\theta \ne 1\}$ and $S = \{a \in \mathbf{Z} : 2(\cos^{8}\theta - \sin^{8}\theta)\sec 2\theta = a^{2},\ \theta \in P\}$. Then $n(S)$ is :
questions.solution:
$2\left(\cos^{8}\theta - \sin^{8}\theta\right)\sec(2\theta) = a^{2}$
$\Rightarrow 2\left(\cos^{4}\theta + \sin^{4}\theta\right)\left(\cos^{2}\theta - \sin^{2}\theta\right)\sec 2\theta = a^{2}$
$\Rightarrow 2\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\sin^{2}2\theta\right) = a^{2}$
$\Rightarrow 2 - \sin^{2}2\theta = a^{2}$
$\Rightarrow \sin^{2}2\theta = 2 - a^{2}$
$\because a \in z$, only possibility $a^{2} = 1$
$\Rightarrow \sin^{2}2\theta = 1$
$\Rightarrow 2\theta = (2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow \theta = (2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{4}$
but at $\theta = (2n + 1)\frac{\pi}{4}$, $\tan^{2}\theta = 1$
so no possible value of $\theta$

questions.stem: Let the vectors $\vec{a} = -\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$. For some $\lambda, \mu \in \mathbf{R}$, let $\vec{c} = \lambda\vec{a} + \mu\vec{b}$. If $\vec{c} \cdot \left(3\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\right) = 10$ and $\vec{c} \cdot \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) = -2$, then $|\vec{c}|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\vec{c} = \lambda\vec{a} + \mu\vec{b}$
$= \lambda(-1, 1, 3) + \mu(1, 3, 1)$
$= (-\lambda + \mu, \lambda + 3\mu, 3\lambda + \mu)$
Now $\vec{c} \cdot (3, -6, 2) = 10$
$\Rightarrow 3(-\lambda + \mu) - 6(\lambda + 3\mu) + 2(3\lambda + \mu) = 10$
$\Rightarrow -3\lambda - 13\mu = 10$
$\Rightarrow 3\lambda + 13\mu = 10$ ..........(i)
and $\vec{c} \cdot (1, 1, 1) = -2$
$\Rightarrow -\lambda + \mu + \lambda + 3\mu + 3\lambda + \mu = -2$
$\Rightarrow 3\lambda + 5\mu = -2$ ...........(ii)
from (i) and (ii)
$\lambda = 1, \mu = -1$
so $\vec{c} = \vec{a} - \vec{b} = (-2, -2, 2)$
$\Rightarrow |\vec{c}|^{2} = 12$

questions.stem: Let the point A be the foot of perpendicular drawn from the point $P(a, b, 0)$ on the line $\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{1} = \frac{z - \alpha}{3}$. If the midpoint of the line segment PA is $\left(0, \frac{3}{4}, \frac{-1}{4}\right)$ then the value of $a^{2} + b^{2} + \alpha^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
(See figure: $P(a, b, 0)$, midpoint $M\left(0, \frac{3}{4}, \frac{-1}{4}\right)$, foot $A\left(-a, \frac{6}{4} - b, -\frac{1}{2}\right)$.)
$\frac{x - 1}{2} = \frac{y - 2}{1} = \frac{z - \alpha}{3} = \lambda$
putting point A in line
$\frac{-a - 1}{2} = \frac{6}{4} - b - 2 = \frac{\frac{-1}{2} - \alpha}{3}$
by solving we get
$a = 0, b = 0, \alpha = 1$
so $a^{2} + b^{2} + \alpha^{2} = 0 + 0 + 1 = 1$

questions.stem: Two adjacent sides of a parallelogram PQRS are given by $\overrightarrow{PQ} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{PS} = \hat{i} - \hat{j}$. If the side PS is rotated about the point P by an acute angle $\alpha$ in the plane of the parallelogram so that it becomes perpendicular to the side PQ, then $\sin^{2}\left(\frac{5\alpha}{2}\right) - \sin^{2}\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
(See figure: parallelogram PQRS with $\overrightarrow{PQ} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, angle SPQ $= 90^\circ - \alpha$, PS rotated by $\alpha$.)
$\cos(90^\circ - \alpha) = \left|\frac{(1, -1, 0) \cdot (0, 1, 1)}{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{2}}\right|$
$= \frac{1}{2}$
$\Rightarrow \sin\alpha = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{\pi}{6}$
Now $\sin^{2}\frac{5\alpha}{2} - \sin^{2}\frac{\alpha}{2}$
$= \sin 3\alpha \cdot \sin 2\alpha$
$= \sin\frac{3\pi}{6} \cdot \sin\frac{2\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

questions.stem: The value of $\int_{0}^{20\pi} \left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x\right)dx$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int_{0}^{20\pi} \left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x\right)dx$
$= 20\int_{0}^{\pi} \left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x\right)dx$
$= 40\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x\right)dx$
$\because \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^{4}x\,dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^{4}x\,dx = \frac{3\pi}{16}$
$\Rightarrow I = 40 \cdot \frac{6\pi}{16} = 15\pi$

questions.stem: Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial of degree 5, and have extrema at $x = 1$ and $x = -1$. If $\lim_{x \to 0}\left(\frac{f(x)}{x^{3}}\right) = -5$, then $f(2) - f(-2)$ is equal to :

Let $f(x) = \int\left(\frac{16x + 24}{x^{2} + 2x - 15}\right)dx$. If $f(4) = 14\log_e 3$ and $f(7) = \log_e(2^{\alpha} \cdot 3^{\beta})$, $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbf{N}$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
$f(x) = \int\left(\frac{16x + 24}{x^{2} + 2x - 15}\right)dx$
$= \int \frac{8(2x + 2) + 8}{x^{2} + 2x - 15}dx$
$= 8\int \frac{2x + 2}{x^{2} + 2x - 15}dx + \int \frac{(x + 5) - (x - 3)}{(x + 5)(x - 3)}dx$
$\Rightarrow f'(x) = 8\ln\left|x^{2} + 2x - 15\right| + \ln\left|\frac{x - 3}{x + 5}\right| + c$
Given $f(4) = 14\ln 3$
$\Rightarrow 14\ln 3 = 8\ln 9 + \ln\left|\frac{1}{9}\right| + c$
$\Rightarrow c = 0$
Now $f(7) = 8\ln 48 - \ln 3$
$= \ln\left(\frac{48^{8}}{3}\right) = \ln\left(2^{32} \cdot 3^{7}\right)$
so $\alpha = 32, \beta = 7$

questions.stem: Let $x = x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $2y^{2}\frac{dx}{dy} - 2xy + x^{2} = 0$, $y > 1$, $x(e) = e$. Then $x(e^{2})$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$2y^{2}\frac{dx}{dy} - 2xy + x^{2} = 0$
$\Rightarrow 2y\frac{(ydx - xdy)}{x^{2}} + dy = 0$
$\Rightarrow -2 \cdot d\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) + \frac{dy}{y} = 0$
$\Rightarrow \frac{-2y}{x} + \ln y = c$
$\because x(e) = e$
$-2 + 1 = c \Rightarrow c = -1$
so $-\frac{2y}{x} + \ln y = -1$
to find $x(e^{2})$ put $y = e^{2}$
$-\frac{2e^{2}}{x} + 2 = -1$
$\Rightarrow \frac{2e^{2}}{x} = 3$
$\Rightarrow x = \frac{2e^{2}}{3}$

questions.stem: Let $A = \{2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$. Let R be a relation on the set $A \times A$ given by $(x, y)R(z, w)$ if and only if x divides z and $y \le w$ Then the number of elements in R is ________.
questions.solution:
$A = \{2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$
$(x, y)\,R\,(z, w)$ if x divides z and $y \le w$
for $x = 2$, $z = 2, 4, 6$
$x = 3$, $z = 3, 6$
$x = 4$, $z = 4$
$x = 5$, $z = 5$
$x = 6$, $z = 6$
and for $y \le w$
total cases $= 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1$
$= 15$
number of elements is $R = 8 \times 15 = 120$

questions.stem: Consider the matrices $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$. If matrices P and Q are such that $PA = B$ and $AQ = B$ then the absolute value of the sum of the diagonal elements of $2(P + Q)$ is ________.
questions.solution:
$A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix}, B = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$
$PA = B$
$\Rightarrow P = BA^{-1}$
$\Rightarrow P = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\frac{1}{4}\begin{bmatrix} -2 & 2 \\ -4 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$
$= \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -21 & 12 \\ -7 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$
$AQ = B$
$\Rightarrow Q = A^{-1}.\ b$
$= \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 9 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$
$= \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} -2 & -6 \\ -5 & -15 \end{bmatrix}$
sum of diagonal elements of $2(P + Q)$
$= 2\left[-\frac{21}{2} + \frac{4}{2} - \frac{2}{2} - \frac{15}{2}\right]$
$= -17 - 17$
$= -34$

questions.stem: Let A be the point $(3, 0)$ and circles with variable diameter AB touch the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 36$ internally. Let the curve C be the locus of the point B. If the eccentricity of C is e, then $72e^{2}$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
(See figure: circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 36$ with $A(3, 0)$ marked.)
Let $B(h, k)$
Circle with AB as diameter
$(x - h)(x - 3) + y(y - k) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} + y^{2} - (h + 3)x - ky + 3h = 0$
Centre $\left(\frac{h + 3}{2}, \frac{k}{2}\right)$
Circle touch internelly so
$c_1c_2 = |r_1 - r_2|$
$\Rightarrow \sqrt{\left(\frac{h + 3}{2}\right)^{2} + \left(\frac{k}{2}\right)^{2}} = 6 - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(h - 3)^{2} + k^{2}}$
$\Rightarrow \sqrt{(x + 3)^{2} + y^{2}} + \sqrt{(x - 3)^{2} + y^{2}} = 12$
$\Rightarrow 2a = 12 \quad \Rightarrow a = 6$ ............(i)
focii are $(-3, 0)$ and $(3, 0)$
$2ae = 6$ ...........(ii)
from (i) and (ii)
$e = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow 72e^{2} = 72 \cdot \frac{1}{4} = 18$

questions.stem: If the area of the region bounded by $16x^{2} - 9y^{2} = 144$ and $8x - 3y = 24$ is A, then $3(A + 6\log_e(3))$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
$16x^{2} - 9y^{2} = 144$
solving it with $8x - 3y = 24$
$16x^{2} - (8x - 24)^{2} = 144$
$\Rightarrow 16x^{2} - 64(x^{2} - 6x + 9) = 144$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} - 4(x^{2} - 6x + 9) = 9$
$\Rightarrow 3x^{2} - 24x + 45 = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} - 8x + 15 = 0$
$\Rightarrow x = 3, 5$
(See figure: region between the right branch of the hyperbola and the line from $(3, 0)$ to $x = 5$.)
Area $= \int_{3}^{5}\left(\sqrt{\frac{16x^{2} - 144}{9}} - \left(\frac{8x - 24}{3}\right)\right)dx$
$= \frac{4}{3}\int_{3}^{5}\left(\sqrt{x^{2} - 9} - \frac{2x}{3} + 18\right)dx$
$= \frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^{2} - 9} - \frac{9}{2}\ln\left|x + \sqrt{x^{2} - 9}\right|\right)_{3}^{5} - \frac{8}{3}\frac{\left(x^{2}\right)_{3}^{5}}{2} + 8(x)_{3}^{5}$
$= \frac{4}{3}\left[\frac{5}{2} \cdot 4 - \frac{9}{2}\ln 9 + \frac{9}{2}\ln 3\right] - \frac{8}{3}\frac{16}{2} + 16$
$= \frac{40}{3} - \frac{9}{2} \cdot \frac{4}{3}\ln 3 - \frac{64}{3} + 16$
$\Rightarrow A = 8 - 6\ln 3$
so $3(A + 6\ln 3)$
$= 3(8 - 6\ln 3 + 6\ln 3) = 24$

questions.stem: The number of points in the interval $[2, 4]$, at which the function $f(x) = \left[x^{2} - x - \frac{1}{2}\right]$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is discontinuous, is ________.
questions.solution:
$f(x) = \left[x^{2} - x - \frac{1}{2}\right]$
let $P(x) = x^{2} - x - \frac{1}{2}$
(See figure: parabola with vertex at $x = \frac{1}{2}$; $P(2) = \frac{3}{2}$, $P(4) = 12 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{23}{2}$.)
so range of $P(x) \leftarrow [1.5, 11.5]$
Total 10 linegers in the range.
so $P(x)$ has 1 x such that
$P(x) = n,\ n \in \{2, 3, \ldots\ldots, 11\}$
$\Rightarrow$ Total 10 discontinuities.
